content.title: About
content.content: Chicken tamale is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a corn‑maize dough (masa) filled with seasoned chicken, spices and sometimes vegetables. The dough is steamed in a banana leaf or corn husk, giving it a moist, fragrant texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tamales are among the oldest foods in the Americas, dating back to the Maya and Aztec civilizations.
They are traditionally prepared in large batches for celebrations such as Day of the Dead and Christmas.
More than 100 regional variations exist, differing in fillings, shapes and cooking methods.
The dough is made from nixtamalized corn flour, which gives tamales their distinctive flavor and texture.
In some regions the filling may include pork, beef, cheese or sweet ingredients in addition to chicken.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The chicken filling provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Tamales contain niacin, vitamin B6 and folate, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: The corn masa adds fiber that aids healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Traditional tamales are not sweetened, making them suitable for moderate consumption.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Both chicken and corn contribute iron, important for blood formation.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn products, which can cause reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Fillings often contain salt and soy sauce, so people on low‑sodium diets should monitor intake.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: Tamales must be cooked thoroughly and cooled quickly; otherwise harmful bacteria can proliferate.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Because of the masa and meat filling, a serving can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tamales are usually served hot, after removing the banana leaf or corn husk. They can be enjoyed on their own or with salsa, guacamole and sour cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked tamales in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them; reheat by steaming or microwaving before serving.
